title: 1:1 prep - Jordan Lee - 2026-03-02
content:
Goals for this 1:1:
- Quick sync on current priorities and blockers (15 min)
- Career check-in: growth goals and next steps (10 min)
- Review action items from last 1:1 and alignment on owner/timeline (10 min)

Notes / context before the meeting:
- Jordan is leading the prefix caching workstream for q1. Deliverables: prototype perf numbers, integration test, and rollout plan. Prototype shows ~18-22% token cost reduction in internal bench but some tail latency regressions on long-seq cases.
- ENG-1423 is the Jira ticket tracking long-seq latency regressions. He raised a potential KV eviction race in the runtime; PR 456 includes initial fixes but needs more test coverage.
- Jordan mentioned bandwidth constraints: balancing deep debugging on the eviction bug vs helping Priya on the canary rollout for quantized LLM variants.

Agenda items and talking points:
1) Blocker triage (15 min)
   - Ask Jordan to summarize current hypothesis for eviction race and what data he still needs.
   - Confirm who else we need on-call for repro. Suggest pairing with Samir this week for focused repro session.
   - Decide whether we pause canary for quantized rollout until eviction fix is validated or proceed with stricter telemetry. My leaning: continue canary but set an automatic rollback threshold for p95 latency + error rate.

2) Roadmap alignment & prioritization (10 min)
   - Confirm priority of prefix-caching vs perf work on KV reclaim. Are we expecting to push any timeline?
   - If prefix-caching rollout depends on eviction fix, get a realistic ETA and communicate to product/console owners.

3) Career / growth check (10 min)
   - Quick feedback: strong ownership on prototype and solid debugging. Need more visibility on cross-team comms (docs + playbook).
   - Discuss interest in leading a small tech talk on caching tradeoffs next month (good for visibility and mentoring).
   - Ask Jordan what stretch areas he wants: architecture reviews, hiring interviews, or ownership of the caching workstream post-rollout.

4) Action items from last 1:1 - quick review (5 min)
   - Jordan to add benchmark harness for long-seq tails - status: in progress (branch: long-seq-harness).
   - Follow-up: raise a short RFC for rollout gating telemetry - I said I'd draft it. TODO: I will add draft RFC by Friday.

Open questions to surface:
- How confident is Jordan in the reproducibility of the eviction race across infra (cloud vs dedicated)? Any env-specific signals?
- Do we have a short-term mitigation that buys time without a full fix? (e.g., more aggressive KV TTL for heavy sequences)
- Who should own post-mortem if the canary triggers rollback? Ops or platform eng? Recommend platform owning post-mortem with SRE assisting.

Concrete action items (owner - due)
- Jordan: run paired repro session with Samir this week and capture minimal reproducer logs - due 2026-03-04.
- Samir: help write e2e test that exercises long-seq eviction paths - due 2026-03-06.
- Aisha (me): draft rollout RFC for canary telemetry + rollback thresholds and share with product + console by 2026-03-05.
- Jordan: prepare 10-min tech talk draft on prefix-caching tradeoffs for internal sync by 2026-03-12.

Follow-ups for next 1:1:
- Status on repro and e2e test.
- Any shifts in timeline for prefix-caching rollout.
- Career item: confirm interest area and agree on 2 concrete steps for next quarter.

Notes to self (manager reminders):
- Encourage more doc-first communication from Jordan; nudge to use the RFC template and link in PRs.
- If eviction repro proves flaky across infra, escalate to infra leads for a focused small working group.
- Keep product informed but avoid overcommitting timelines; frame as dependent on KV fix.

Rough meeting script (start to finish)
- Start: quick personal check-in (2 min)
- Blocker deep-dive (12 min)
- Roadmap & prioritization (8 min)
- Career + growth (8 min)
- Review and confirm action items (5 min)

Quick links I may reference during the 1:1:
- ENG-1423: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/ENG-1423
- PR 456: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/456
- Confluence draft: KV-Cache Optimizations - https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/KV-Cache-Optimizations

End of notes.
